The available Scion Navigation System (SNS)(1) offers a wide range of features to help keep you on track when
you’re out and about. Not only does the SNS help you find where you’re going by using a point of interest,
address information, intersection, coordinate, or freeway search, it also doubles as an audio system. Plus,
when you’re not moving, you can take advantage of the SNS DVD capabilities to watch your favorite videos on
the LCD screen. With Alpine Digital Sound Processing (DSP), you choose from five different preset equalizer
curves or create your own - making sure that wherever you’re headed, you control the soundscape.
visit http://scion.com/sns for more information

ABs (if installed) are designed to inflate only under certain conditions and in certain types of severe collisions: frontal and knee ABs typically inflate in frontal collisions; side
and side curtain ABs in side collisions; Roll-Sensing Curtain ABs at a severe tilt degree, roll or lateral G-force. In all other accidents, the ABs will not inflate. To decrease the
risk of injury from an inflating AB, always wear seatbelts, sit upright in the middle of the seat as far back as possible and do not lean against the door. Do not put objects in front
of an AB or around the seatback. Do not use a rearward-facing child seat in any front passenger seat. The force of an inflating AB may cause serious injury or death. See your
Owner’s Manual for further information/warnings. (5) The Direct Tire Pressure Monitor System alerts the driver when tire pressure is critically low. For optimal tire wear and
performance, tire pressure should be checked regularly with a gauge; do not rely solely on the monitor system. See your Owner’s Manual for details. (6) Vehicle Stability Control
(VSC) is an electronic system designed to help the driver maintain vehicle control under adverse conditions. It is not a substitute for safe driving practices. Factors including
speed, road conditions, and driver steering input can affect whether VSC will be effective in preventing a loss of control. Please see your Owner’s Manual for further details.
(7) Brake Assist is designed to help the driver take full advantage of the benefits of ABS. It is not a substitute for safe driving practices. Braking effectiveness also depends on
proper brake-system maintenance and tire and road conditions. (8) Active Head Rests can help prevent or limit the extent of whiplash in certain types of rear-end collisions.
